image_description: A vintage black typewriter viewed from a high angle. The image shows the carriage, platen, and the keyboard deck with round white keys. The focus is on the entire machine rather than a specific component.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated rectangular key spanning the full width of the bottom keyboard row.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays a full typewriter, not an isolated space bar. While a space bar exists on the device, it does not span the 'full width' of the row (it is flanked by other keys), and the subject of the image is the whole machine, not the key itself.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Length is dramatically greater than any other key, roughly ten times the width of a standard letter key.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: On this specific vintage typewriter, the space bar is only slightly wider than the round letter keys, not 'dramatically greater' or 10x the width as described in the modern keyboard taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface is flat or slightly concave.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible keys are round and convex (domed), typical of vintage typewriters, contradicting the flat/concave description of a modern space bar.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Underside connects to a long stabilizer bar mechanism.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the key is completely occluded by the keyboard deck; the internal mechanism is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Label is typically blank with no printed character.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar (center bottom) appears blank, consistent with the checkpoint, though this is a minor feature in the context of the whole image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Positioned centrally between modifier keys on the bottom row.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is located in the correct relative position on the keyboard deck.
The keys appear to be made of hard plastic or bakelite with a slight sheen, but the dominant material of the image is the painted metal body of the typewriter, not just the plastic key.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Typically white, black, or gray to match keyboard color scheme.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The key is white/off-white, matching the other keys.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Part of a standard computer or typewriter keyboard.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object is indeed part of a typewriter keyboard.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The mechanical structure of the typewriter carriage is nonsensical. The metal arms and the platen roller blend into each other without clear joints or logical mechanical connectivity. The ribbon guide area is a fused mess of black shapes.

The round keys lack distinct edges and individual shadows. They appear to bleed into the black keyboard deck, looking like white dots painted on a surface rather than physical 3D objects sitting in slots.

artifact_observations.location: Right side of the typewriter body
artifact_observations.reasoning: The right edge of the typewriter base warps unnaturally. The perspective lines do not converge logically, giving the impression that the object is melting or bending in 3D space.

alignment_reasoning: The image fails significantly as a representation of the class 'space bar'. It depicts a whole typewriter rather than the specific component. Furthermore, the geometry of the space bar shown (vintage style) contradicts the taxonomy's definition of a modern elongated rectangular key (flat, 10x width). Only positional and labeling checkpoints are met.
artifact_reasoning: The image exhibits moderate-to-severe AI artifacts. The mechanical components of the typewriter suffer from structural collapse and fusion, lacking logical assembly. The keyboard keys show texture anomalies where they fail to separate cleanly from the background, and there is noticeable perspective warping on the chassis.
